originalTitle: Australia politics live: Coalition to work with Hanson on migration bill; Greens fear PM ‘under the thumb’ of gambling lobby
content: Work from home laws won’t come into effect in Victoria until after election The Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, has announced the government’s nation-first bill to legislate a right to work from home two days a week won’t take effect until after the election. Carroll also said debate on the bill - which was expected to pass parliament’s upper house later this week - has been delayed. He said he made the decision as part of his commitment to “reset the relationship” with the business community: I’ve spoken with Sally Curtin this morning and Tim Piper, and I told them that work from home will not proceed on the 1st of September. It will proceed on the 1st of July in 2027. I want to be very clear. I support work from home. I support flexible work. It is good for working families. Equally, though, we need to make sure that ...Everyone knows it’s a partnership between working families and the business community and the government. ‘This government has been beaten by high interest and inflation’: Taylor Angus Taylor is giving his party room a bit of a gee up for the first sitting day back after the winter break. He’s let the cameras in for his opening speech (the same as what Anthony Albanese did ahead of his caucus meeting yesterday) – before the party gets into the nitty gritty. We can expect gambling to be a key talking point of the meeting. There are plenty of shouts of “hear hear” from the MPs in the background. Taylor says: This government told Australians that it had beaten high inflation and high interest rates and this government has been beaten by high inflation and high interest rates. Now, over the course of the break, we launched our plan. Our plan to fix the economy and to protect our way of life. As I said, we will lax labor’s toxic taxes, their taxes on savings, on investment, on housing, on small businesses, on widows. That last point is reference to the so-called “widow tax”. Under the tax reforms announced in the May budget, a widow or divorcee would lose grandfathered exemptions to negative gearing and capital gains tax in the event the property was transferred from both to one of the partners and the tax settings reset. Independent senator David Pocock raised the issue before the tax legislation was passed, which then Labor said it would fix in subsequent bills. Albanese to meet with Vietnam’s president at Parliament House The president and general secretary of Vietnam, To Lam, is in Canberra today, currently meeting with the governor general, Sam Mostyn. Lam arrived in Sydney yesterday, in time for the government to announce that VietJet would start flying into the new western Sydney airport. The president will then head over to Parliament House to meet with Anthony Albanese and the pair will later provide joint statements to the media. We can probably expect China and Donald Trump to be on the agenda for the talks. Malinauskas didn’t consult with federal counterparts on AI royal commission Yesterday’s announcement that South Australia would hold a royal commission into artificial intelligence would have taken some by surprise yesterday – including the federal government. The SA premier, Peter Malinauskas, has done his own media rounds this morning plugging the announcement, but says he didn’t give the commonwealth a heads up. He told RN Breakfast the idea for a royal commission was cemented after he went to the United States: Within 72 hours of being on the ground and talking to people who are themselves developing the technology and using the technology, and them talking about the profound implications of what AI will do to our modern economy, I was absolutely convinced this is something we should do ... This is something that we’re pursuing as a state government because of course within our federation sub-national governments or states are responsible for a whole range of areas of service delivery that are quite separate to considerations of the federal government. Earlier, independent MP Kate Chaney told RN Breakfast it was good the premier was “realising the magnitude of this issue” but said a royal commission wasn’t the right mechanism. It’s very slow, takes too long. I wrote a letter to the Coalition and some others a few weeks ago pushing for or seeking support for a joint standing committee on AI because I do think we need parliamentary oversight … But Peter Malinauskas has at least recognised the urgency of this issue. Speaking of One Nation’s immigration bill, Ted O’Brien tells News24 that he’s open to working with “anybody who is going to make Australia safer.” He says the Coalition are working on their own immigration bill, and that the opposition “won’t be political” in dealing with the issue. We are open to working with anybody who is going to make Australia safer. I don’t particularly care where they come from. We’re yet to see all the detail, right? So if, at the end of the day, ours is a better bill, of course, we’ll be pursuing ours over it but I think the right thing to do by Australia is not to be overly political on these issues. If somebody wants to genuinely bring forward a bill, absolutely, let’s engage in good faith, have a look at it. In two separate cases in June 2022 and in November 2023, the high court struck down Coalition-era laws that gave the home affairs minister power to strip dual nationals of Australian citizenship for engaging in suspected terrorist activities. The shadow home affairs minister, Jonno Duniam, also told News24 this morning that the Coalition would work with One Nation on the bill: We’ll work with them on that legislation, it is important we get it right. We’d love to see it go off to a Senate committee to make sure that people who know a little more than we in the Senate know, legal experts to make sure it is robust. We want to shut the door on terrorists, we’ve been trying for years to do this. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚政治直播：联盟将与汉森合作制定移民法案；绿党担心首相“受到赌博游说团的控制”
chineseContent: 维多利亚州的在家工作法要等到选举后才会生效维多利亚州州长本·卡罗尔(Ben Carroll)宣布，政府第一个立法规定每周在家工作两天的权利的法案要到选举后才会生效。卡罗尔还表示，对该法案的辩论预计将在本周晚些时候在议会上院通过，但已被推迟。他说，他做出这一决定是他与商界“重建关系”承诺的一部分：今天早上我已经与 Sally Curtin 和 Tim Piper 进行了交谈，我告诉他们 9 月 1 日不会继续在家工作。它将在 2027 年 7 月 1 日进行。我想非常明确。我支持在家工作。我支持弹性工作。这对于工薪家庭来说是有好处的。但同样，我们需要确保……每个人都知道这是工薪家庭、商界和政府之间的合作伙伴关系。 “这个政府已经被高利率和通货膨胀击败了”：泰勒·安格斯·泰勒（Taylor Angus Taylor）正在为寒假后的第一天的聚会提供一些振奋人心的空间。在党进入实质内容之前，他让摄像机进入他的开场演讲（与昨天安东尼·艾博尼斯在党团会议之前所做的一样）。我们可以预期赌博将成为会议的一个关键话题。背景中有很多国会议员发出的“听听”的喊声。泰勒说：本届政府告诉澳大利亚人，它已经击败了高通胀和高利率，而本届政府也被高通胀和高利率击败了。现在，在休息期间，我们启动了我们的计划。我们的计划是修复经济并保护我们的生活方式。正如我所说，我们将放松对劳工的有毒税和储蓄税
